title: Constrain a path number
summary: Symfony: Constrain a path number. Visit /double/cat.
introduction: A route requirement describes allowed path text. Open GET /double/4.
learningObjectives: Constrain a path number with Symfony

blocks.text: Create a Symfony 7 skeleton project with Composer and install the Symfony CLI. Save each example as src/Controller/LessonController.php. Use the default attribute route import. Run symfony server:start --no-tls --port=8000.

blocks.title: Constrain a path number
blocks.code:
<?php
namespace App\Controller;
use Symfony\Bundle\FrameworkBundle\Controller\AbstractController;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\JsonResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse;
use Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route;
class LessonController extends AbstractController {
#[Route("/double/{n}", requirements: ["n" => "[0-9]+"], methods: ["GET"])]
public function twice(int $n): JsonResponse { return new JsonResponse(["answer" => $n * 2]); }
}

blocks.text: The route requirement allows the digits in 4. Symfony supplies the typed input to the method.

blocks.title: Watch out
blocks.text: A requirement controls route matching, not every allowed data range.
